comparator.name: Spanish Language and Culture
comparator.route: Transatlantic Perspectives on Spain and Latin America
comparator.sourceNotes: The standard Spanish track includes a 127.5 EC major and 52.5 EC of electives. This example follows the published rotation for students starting in 2026. It includes a Spanish-language thesis and keeps the 30 EC elective package and 22.5 EC of other electives open.

components.name: Español 1
components.note: First course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR A1.

components.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
components.note: Introduces methods for interpreting literary texts.

components.name: Español 2
components.note: Second course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR A2.

components.name: Comparative Morphosyntax
components.note: Compares how languages form words and sentences.

components.name: Español 3
components.note: Third course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR B1.

components.name: Teatro, cine e intermedialidad: España y América Latina
components.note: Studies theater and cinema in Spain and Latin America and how they interact with other media.

components.name: Español 4
components.note: Fourth course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR B2.

components.name: Sociolingüística: España y América Latina
components.note: Studies Spanish in its social contexts in Spain and Latin America.

components.name: Competencias de lectura y conciencia cultural: España y América Latina
components.note: Develops reading skills and cultural awareness through material from Spain and Latin America.

components.name: Migration and Diaspora
components.note: Studies migration and diaspora in the Transatlantic Perspectives package.

components.name: Testimonios, crónicas, representaciones: España y América Latina
components.note: Studies testimonies, chronicles and representation in Spain and Latin America.

components.name: Variation and Change in Language
components.note: Examines how language varies and changes.

components.name: Research Methods Intercultural Communication
components.note: An approved research methods choice focused on intercultural communication.

components.name: Other Profiling Electives
components.note: Electives beyond the 30 EC package, subject to Utrecht’s degree rules.

components.name: Lengua, cultura e identidad: España y América Latina
components.note: One of two additional advanced courses. It examines language, culture and identity in Spain and Latin America.

components.name: Contesting the Past
components.note: One of two additional advanced courses. It examines contested interpretations of the past.

components.name: Taller de escritura profesional, creativa y académica
components.note: Develops professional, creative and academic writing in Spanish and prepares students for the thesis.

components.name: Spanish Language and Culture Thesis
components.note: Students carry out an independent research project and write the thesis in Spanish.

components.name: Coherent Elective Package
components.note: A coherent elective package, such as a minor or approved study abroad.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Transatlantic Perspectives on Spain and Latin America
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The standard track represents the broad degree through study of Spanish and of Spain and Latin America. The 2026 intake is scheduled for the four odd-year courses in year two. The two first listed even-year courses meet the additional depth requirement in year three. Research Methods Intercultural Communication is an approved choice that supports the track’s study of migration and cultural identity. Crossing Borders is a separate eligible track.

cellNotes.text: Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR A1 at this stage.
Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR A2 at this stage.
Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR B1 at this stage.
Utrecht’s sequence develops Spanish proficiency through CEFR B2 at this stage.
Utrecht compares how languages structure words and sentences. UCR’s stylistics course examines how choices in language create effects in texts.
Utrecht studies Spanish in its social contexts in Spain and Latin America.
Utrecht studies language variation and change as a dedicated subject.
Utrecht examines the relationship between language and identity in Spain and Latin America.
Utrecht’s Spanish-language writing workshop prepares students for their thesis.
Both introduce methods for interpreting literary texts. UCR’s course surveys literature across traditions.
Both examine how stories move between media. UCR focuses on literature and film adaptation, while Utrecht also studies theater from Spain and Latin America.
Utrecht connects reading skills and cultural awareness with the Spanish-speaking world.
Utrecht focuses on testimony, chronicles and representation from Spain and Latin America. UCR’s life writing course spans a wider range of settings.
Both consider contested readings of history. UCR studies Indigenous North American histories, colonial violence and resistance.
Utrecht includes dedicated study of migration and diaspora. Migrant solidarity is one topic within UCR’s broader social theory course.
Utrecht’s methods course focuses on intercultural communication. UCR teaches qualitative research methods for a wider range of social questions.
Students choose these electives under Utrecht’s degree rules.
Utrecht requires a 7.5 EC thesis written in Spanish. The optional UCR research element sits outside the 180 EC schedule.
Students can complete a minor or another approved package such as study abroad.
